claim: About 150 uPNs constituting 58 glomeruli in the antennal lobe (AL) are bundled together in the axonal extension, routing the olfactory signal received at AL to mushroom body (MB) calyx and lateral horn (LH).
source: About 150 uPNs constituting 58 glomeruli in the antennal lobe (AL) are bundled together in the axonal extension, routing the olfactory signal received at AL to mushroom body (MB) calyx and lateral horn (LH).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the anatomical structure and connectivity of uPNs based on the EM reconstruction data.

claim: The homotypic uPNs that constitute glomeruli are tightly bundled and stereotyped in position throughout the neuropils.
source: The homotypic uPNs that constitute glomeruli are tightly bundled and stereotyped in position throughout the neuropils, even though the glomerular PN organization in AL is no longer sustained in the higher brain center.
evidence: This claim is supported by the inter-PN distance analysis and clustering results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The glomerular PN organization in AL is no longer sustained in the higher brain center.
source: The homotypic uPNs that constitute glomeruli are tightly bundled and stereotyped in position throughout the neuropils, even though the glomerular PN organization in AL is no longer sustained in the higher brain center.
evidence: This is based on the observation that while homotypic uPNs remain bundled, the glomerular structure itself is not maintained in MB calyx and LH.

claim: Odor-type dependent clusters consisting of multiple homotypes innervate the MB calyx and LH.
source: Instead, odor-type dependent clusters consisting of multiple homotypes innervate the MB calyx and LH.
evidence: This is demonstrated through hierarchical clustering analysis and statistical tests showing associations between spatial organization and odor types.

claim: Pheromone-encoding and hygro/thermo-sensing homotypes are spatially segregated in MB calyx.
source: Pheromone-encoding and hygro/thermo-sensing homotypes are spatially segregated in MB calyx, whereas two distinct clusters of food-related homotypes are found in LH in addition to the segregation of pheromone-encoding and hygro/thermo-sensing homotypes.
evidence: This is supported by the clustering analysis and visualization of uPN organization in MB calyx shown in Figure 3.

claim: Two distinct clusters of food-related homotypes are found in LH in addition to the segregation of pheromone-encoding and hygro/thermo-sensing homotypes.
source: Pheromone-encoding and hygro/thermo-sensing homotypes are spatially segregated in MB calyx, whereas two distinct clusters of food-related homotypes are found in LH in addition to the segregation of pheromone-encoding and hygro/thermo-sensing homotypes.
evidence: This is demonstrated through the clustering analysis of uPNs in LH shown in Figure 4.

claim: There are statistically significant associations between the spatial organization among a group of homotypic uPNs and certain stereotyped olfactory responses.
source: We find that there are statistically significant associations between the spatial organization among a group of homotypic uPNs and certain stereotyped olfactory responses.
evidence: This is supported by Pearson's χ²-test results and mutual information analysis presented in Appendix 1.

claim: The signals from some of the tightly bundled homotypes converge to a specific group of lateral horn neurons (LHNs).
source: Additionally, the signals from some of the tightly bundled homotypes converge to a specific group of lateral horn neurons (LHNs), which indicates that homotype (or odor type) specific integration of signals occurs at the synaptic interface between PNs and LHNs.
evidence: This is demonstrated through connectivity analysis between uPNs and LHNs shown in Figures 10, 11, and 12.

claim: Homotype (or odor type) specific integration of signals occurs at the synaptic interface between PNs and LHNs.
source: Additionally, the signals from some of the tightly bundled homotypes converge to a specific group of lateral horn neurons (LHNs), which indicates that homotype (or odor type) specific integration of signals occurs at the synaptic interface between PNs and LHNs.
evidence: This is inferred from the connectivity patterns observed in the common synapse matrices and homotype-specific connections.

claim: Some of the olfactory information are already encoded in the spatial organization of uPNs before neural computation in the inner brain.
source: Our findings suggest that before neural computation in the inner brain, some of the olfactory information are already encoded in the spatial organization of uPNs, illuminating that a certain degree of labeled-line strategy is at work in the Drosophila olfactory system.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed associations between spatial organization and odor types, as well as the connectivity patterns.

claim: A certain degree of labeled-line strategy is at work in the Drosophila olfactory system.
source: Our findings suggest that before neural computation in the inner brain, some of the olfactory information are already encoded in the spatial organization of uPNs, illuminating that a certain degree of labeled-line strategy is at work in the Drosophila olfactory system.
evidence: This is supported by the observation of homotype-specific connections, spatial segregation of certain odor types, and convergence patterns to third-order neurons.

claim: PNs bridge the olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) in the antenna and maxillary palp to higher olfactory centers where neural computation occurs for Drosophila to sense and perceive the environment.
source: It is the PNs that bridge the olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) in the antenna and maxillary palp to higher olfactory centers where neural computation occurs for Drosophila to sense and perceive the environment (Hallem and Carlson, 2004a).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citation to Hallem and Carlson, 2004a.

claim: The uniglomerular PNs (uPNs) in AL constitute glomeruli that collect olfactory signals from ORNs of the same receptor type.
source: The uniglomerular PNs (uPNs) in AL constitute glomeruli that collect olfactory signals from ORNs of the same receptor type (Gao et al., 2000; Couto et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gao et al., 2000 and Couto et al., 2005.

claim: uPNs innervating MB calyx and LH relay the signals further inside the brain through synaptic junctions with the Kenyon cells (KCs) and lateral horn neurons (LHNs), respectively.
source: uPNs innervating MB calyx and LH relay the signals further inside the brain through synaptic junctions with the Kenyon cells (KCs) and lateral horn neurons (LHNs), respectively.
evidence: This is a description of the known anatomical connectivity in the Drosophila olfactory system.

claim: Multiglomerular PNs (mPNs) innervate multiple glomeruli, often contributing to the inhibitory regulation of signals relayed from ORNs to third-order olfactory neurons.
source: Multiglomerular PNs (mPNs), on the other hand, innervate multiple glomeruli, often contributing to the inhibitory regulation of signals relayed from ORNs to third-order olfactory neurons (Berck et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Berck et al., 2016.

claim: Many GABAergic PNs tend to bypass MB calyx while innervating multiple glomeruli in AL (and hence are mPNs).
source: PNs can functionally be categorized into either excitatory (cholinergic) or inhibitory (GABAergic), where a many GABAergic PNs tend to bypass MB calyx while innervating multiple glomeruli in AL (and hence are mPNs) (Schultzhaus et al., 2017; Shimizu and Stopfer, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schultzhaus et al., 2017 and Shimizu and Stopfer, 2017.

claim: Hierarchical clustering on the distance matrix for uPNs in MB calyx from the FAFB dataset results in 10 clusters.
source: In MB calyx, the hierarchical clustering divides the uPNs from the FAFB dataset into 10 clusters (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a direct result from the clustering analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Hierarchical clustering on the distance matrix for uPNs in LH from the FAFB dataset results in 11 clusters.
source: In LH, 11 clusters are identified in the FAFB dataset (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a direct result from the clustering analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: uPNs sharing the same glomerular label are grouped under a common branch in the dendrogram constructed from the distance matrix for the uPNs at AL.
source: This is apparent in the dendrogram constructed from the distance matrix for the uPNs at AL (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), where uPNs sharing the same glomerular label are grouped under a common branch, thereby demonstrating the spatial proximity between uPNs forming the same glomerulus.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The same hierarchical clustering analysis performed on the hemibrain dataset results in 14 clusters for uPN innervation in MB calyx and 13 clusters in LH.
source: The same hierarchical clustering analysis performed on the hemibrain dataset results in 14 clusters for uPN innervation in MB calyx and 13 clusters in LH.
evidence: This is stated as a result from analyzing the hemibrain dataset.

claim: Spatial and structural characteristics of individual clusters observed from the FAFB dataset are well translated and comparable to those from the hemibrain dataset.
source: Despite the differences in the number of clusters, we find that spatial and structural characteristics of individual clusters observed from the FAFB dataset are well translated and comparable to those from the hemibrain dataset (see the clustering result in Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing clustering results from both datasets shown in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: A higher degree of overlapping in MB calyx carries over to the uPN organization in LH.
source: This implies that a higher degree of overlapping in MB calyx carries over to the uPN organization in LH.
evidence: This is inferred from the positive correlation between λX values in MB calyx and LH.

claim: The organization of olfactory uPNs varies greatly in the three neuropils.
source: Taken together, the organization of olfactory uPNs varies greatly in the three neuropils.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the differences in d̄intra, d̄inter, and λ values across the three neuropils.

claim: The clear homotype-to-homotype segregation in AL no longer holds in MB calyx.
source: The clear homotype-to-homotype segregation in AL no longer holds in MB calyx.
evidence: This is concluded from the increased λ values and decreased d̄inter values in MB calyx compared to AL.

claim: For some homotypes, the well-segregated organizations in AL are recovered when they reach LH.
source: For some homotypes, the well-segregated organizations in AL are recovered when they reach LH (compare Figure 7A and Figure 7B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing the scatter plots in Figure 7A and Figure 7B.

claim: Most of the KCs and LHNs integrate information from multiple homotypes.
source: It is observed that most of the KCs and LHNs integrate information from multiple homotypes, but that there are also a small number of KCs and LHNs that synapse only with a single homotype (Figure 10).
evidence: This is shown in the connectivity analysis presented in Figure 10.

claim: There are a small number of KCs and LHNs that synapse only with a single homotype.
source: It is observed that most of the KCs and LHNs integrate information from multiple homotypes, but that there are also a small number of KCs and LHNs that synapse only with a single homotype (Figure 10).
evidence: This is shown in the homotype-specific connections analysis in Figure 10.

claim: Homotype-specific connections are much more prevalent in LHNs compared to KCs.
source: Compared to those in KCs, the 'homotype-specific' connections are much more prevalent in LHNs (Figure 10).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing Figure 10A and Figure 10B.

claim: The homotype-specific connections tend to increase under a more stringent synapse selection criterion, especially in LH.
source: Figure 10—figure supplement 1 demonstrates that the homotype-specific connections tend to increase under a more stringent synapse selection criterion, especially in LH.
evidence: This is shown by comparing Figure 10 with Figure 10—figure supplement 1 using different synaptic thresholds.

claim: The existence of homotype-specific third-order neurons suggests that a subset of olfactory processing may rely on the labeled-line strategy that extends beyond the layer of second-order neurons to the higher brain center.
source: The existence of these 'homotype-specific' third-order neurons suggests that a subset of olfactory processing may rely on the labeled-line strategy that extends beyond the layer of second-order neurons to the higher brain center.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of homotype-specific connections in the connectivity analysis.

claim: The synaptic connections at the PN-KC interface in MB calyx are largely integrative and randomized - with an exception of hygro/thermo-sensing homotypes that display stereotypy even in terms of the connectivity to the KCs.
source: The synaptic connections at the PN-KC interface in MB calyx are largely integrative and randomized - with an exception of hygro/thermo-sensing homotypes that display stereotypy even in terms of the connectivity to the KCs.
evidence: This is concluded from the connectivity analysis and comparison with spatial clustering shown in Figure 12A.

claim: A similar observation has been made by Li et al., 2020, who employed NBLAST score to identify a structural segregation between odor-encoding and hygro/thermo-sensing homotypes.
source: A similar observation has been made by Li et al., 2020, who employed NBLAST score to identify a structural segregation between odor-encoding and hygro/thermo-sensing homotypes.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Li et al., 2020.

claim: Li et al., 2020 found that specific KC types are preferentially targeted by hygro/thermo-sensing homotypes.
source: They found that specific KC types are preferentially targeted by hygro/thermo-sensing homotypes.
evidence: This is a finding from Li et al., 2020 cited in the manuscript.

claim: The connectivity-based clustering at MB calyx appears less structured than the spatial proximity-based clustering.
source: Upon visual inspection, the connectivity-based clustering at MB calyx (Figure 12A on the right) appears less structured than the spatial proximity-based clustering (Figure 12A on the left).
evidence: This is observed by comparing the two dendrograms in Figure 12A.

claim: The spatially well-clustered uPNs at MB calyx (or stereotyped structure) do not necessarily translate into structured connectivity patterns (or stereotyped connectivity).
source: Therefore, the spatially well-clustered uPNs at MB calyx (or stereotyped structure) do not necessarily translate into structured connectivity patterns (or stereotyped connectivity), which is consistent with the notion of randomized PN-KC connections (Caron et al., 2013; Stevens, 2015; Eichler et al., 2017; Zheng et al., 2020).
evidence: This is concluded from the tanglegram analysis in Figure 12A and is consistent with previous literature.

claim: Most homotypic uPNs are grouped in the connectivity-based clustering for LH.
source: In stark contrast to the outcomes for MB calyx, most homotypic uPNs are grouped in the connectivity-based clustering for LH (Figure 12B).
evidence: This is observed in the tanglegram for LH shown in Figure 12B.

claim: The spatially proximal uPNs synapse with a similar group of LHNs.
source: This suggests that the spatially proximal uPNs synapse with a similar group of LHNs.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that homotypic uPNs are grouped together in both spatial and connectivity-based clustering for LH.

claim: The stereotyped organization and stereotyped connectivity of uPNs in LH have been suggested before.
source: The stereotyped organization and stereotyped connectivity of uPNs in LH have been suggested before (Jefferis et al., 2007; Liang et al., 2013; Kohl et al., 2013; Fişek and Wilson, 2014), and we demonstrate such stereotypies are, in reality, expressed throughout LH over all uPNs.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Stereotypies in organization and connectivity are expressed throughout LH over all uPNs.
source: The stereotyped organization and stereotyped connectivity of uPNs in LH have been suggested before (Jefferis et al., 2007; Liang et al., 2013; Kohl et al., 2013; Fişek and Wilson, 2014), and we demonstrate such stereotypies are, in reality, expressed throughout LH over all uPNs.
evidence: This is demonstrated through the tanglegram analysis in Figure 12B showing alignment between spatial and connectivity-based clustering.

claim: In LH, spatial and organizational characteristics of uPNs are well translated to connectivity to LHNs.
source: In LH, spatial and organizational characteristics of uPNs are well translated to connectivity to LHNs.
evidence: This is concluded from the tanglegram analysis and statistical comparisons in Appendix 2.

claim: The inter-PN organization revealed in this study and its association with odor type/valence are reminiscent of the generally accepted notion that the form determines the function in biology.
source: The inter-PN organization revealed in this study and its association with odor type/valence are reminiscent of the generally accepted notion that the form determines the function in biology.
evidence: This is a general principle in biology that the authors relate to their findings.

claim: Previously observed stereotypes of neurons in the Drosophila olfactory system were largely based on the differentiation between pheromones and non-pheromones.
source: Previously observed stereotypes of neurons in the Drosophila olfactory system were largely based on the differentiation between pheromones and non-pheromones (Ruta et al., 2010; Kohl et al., 2013; Frechter et al., 2019; Das Chakraborty and Sachse, 2021), the whole-cell patch-clamp recording (Seki et al., 2017), and imaging studies suggestive of stimulus-dependent arrangement of neurons in LH (Marin et al., 2002; Wong et al., 2002; Jefferis et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The results are generally consistent with previous studies, which suggest that a level of stereotypy in uPN organization in MB calyx and LH is universal throughout Drosophila.
source: Our results are generally consistent with the previous studies, which suggest that a level of stereotypy in uPN organization in MB calyx and LH is universal throughout Drosophila, which can be captured through different metrics and methodologies.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the current results with previous literature.

claim: The clustering results in LH share similarities with the NBLAST score-based LH clusters.
source: Our clustering results in LH share similarities with the NBLAST score-based LH clusters (Bates et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with results from Bates et al., 2020.

claim: The inter-PN distances and clustering results suggest the spatial organization of uPNs differs greatly in each neuropil.
source: Our inter-PN distances and clustering results suggest the spatial organization of uPNs differs greatly in each neuropil (Figure 5).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the analysis presented in Figure 5.

claim: Some of the tightly bundled organization of uPN homotypes are well preserved throughout the neuropils despite the lack of glomerulus in MB calyx and LH.
source: Some of the tightly bundled organization of uPN homotypes are well preserved throughout the neuropils despite the lack of glomerulus in MB calyx and LH.
evidence: This is concluded from the d̄intra values being comparable across neuropils.

claim: The spatial segregation between different homotypes is practically not present in MB calyx, leading to a high degree of overlapping.
source: The spatial segregation between different homotypes is, however, practically not present in MB calyx, leading to a high degree of overlapping.
evidence: This is concluded from the high λ values in MB calyx.

claim: The heterogeneity of homotypes at the PN-KC synaptic interface may physically assist the randomized sampling known to exist between uPNs and KCs.
source: Therefore, the heterogeneity of homotypes at the PN-KC synaptic interface may physically assist the randomized sampling known to exist between uPNs and KCs (Caron et al., 2013; Stevens, 2015; Eichler et al., 2017; Zheng et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed high degree of overlapping in MB calyx and previous literature on randomized PN-KC connections.

claim: LH is compartmentalized into four regions based on odor types.
source: Our analysis suggests that LH is compartmentalized into four regions: (1) Posterior-dorsal region primarily occupied by food-related uPNs; (2) Anterior-ventral region occupied by pheromone-encoding uPNs; (3) Biforked bundle surrounding posterior-dorsal region largely occupied by food-related uPNs with an aversive response; (4) Posterior-ventral-medial region occupied by hygro/thermo-sensing uPNs.
evidence: This is concluded from the clustering analysis and odor type associations shown in Figure 4 and Figure 8.

claim: The three domains (LH-PM, LH-AM, and LH-AL) suggested by Strutz et al., 2014 seem to be a different combination of the clustering result from the current study.
source: Previous attempts at identifying regions of odorant space in LH revealed compatible results. The three domains (LH-PM, LH-AM, and LH-AL) suggested by Strutz et al., 2014 seem to be a different combination of our clustering result (LH-PM and LH-AM correspond to the posterior-dorsal region and LH-AL corresponds to a combination of anterior-ventral region and the biforked bundle).
evidence: This is a comparison with results from Strutz et al., 2014.

claim: The study of the axo-axonic communities in LH yields results with comparable characteristics to the current study.
source: Although not perfect, the study of the axo-axonic communities in LH yields results with comparable characteristics (Bates et al., 2020), understandably due to the necessity of inter-neuronal proximity to form synapses.
evidence: This is a comparison with results from Bates et al., 2020.

claim: Many homotypic uPNs that are spatially localized in LH can be associated with key survival features and a strong innate response.
source: Many homotypic uPNs that are spatially localized in LH can be associated with key survival features and a strong innate response (Seki et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Seki et al., 2017.

claim: The study lends support to the existing studies pointing to the labeled-line strategy in the Drosophila olfactory system.
source: Our study not only lends support to the existing studies pointing to the labeled-line strategy in the Drosophila olfactory system but also suggests that there may exist an even more sophisticated level of spatial organization, which supersedes the pheromone versus non-pheromone segregation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed spatial organization and connectivity patterns.

claim: There may exist an even more sophisticated level of spatial organization, which supersedes the pheromone versus non-pheromone segregation.
source: Our study not only lends support to the existing studies pointing to the labeled-line strategy in the Drosophila olfactory system but also suggests that there may exist an even more sophisticated level of spatial organization, which supersedes the pheromone versus non-pheromone segregation.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed clustering patterns that go beyond simple pheromone/non-pheromone distinctions.

claim: While the spatial organization of uPNs in LH has a basis on the functionality of the odor type encoded, it does not seem to be directly translated to segregated chemical features seen in LHNs.
source: Interestingly, while the spatial organization of uPNs in LH has a basis on the functionality of the odor type encoded, it does not seem to be directly translated to segregated chemical features seen in LHNs (Frechter et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an observation comparing the current results with findings from Frechter et al., 2019.

claim: The apparent divergence observed at the PN-LHN interface, coupled with strongly stereotyped connectivity may contribute to a higher resolution of odor categorization.
source: The apparent divergence observed at the PN-LHN interface, coupled with strongly stereotyped connectivity may contribute to a higher resolution of odor categorization.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed connectivity patterns.

claim: The results from both the FAFB and hemibrain datasets are generally consistent.
source: Our analyses of both the FAFB and the hemibrain dataset (Scheffer et al., 2020) find that the results from both datasets are generally consistent.
evidence: This is stated as a general conclusion from comparing analyses of both datasets.

claim: The outcomes from analyses of the two EM datasets lend support to the previous claims of stereotypy in the Drosophila brain and neuronal structures.
source: In conclusion, the outcomes from our analyses of the two EM datasets lend support to the previous claims of stereotypy in the Drosophila brain and neuronal structures (Jenett et al., 2012; Jeanne et al., 2018; Schlegel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a conclusion supported by the consistency between the two datasets and citations to previous studies.

claim: While the primary connectivity motif of third-order olfactory neurons indeed integrates signals, there still exist several labeled lines.
source: Our study suggests that while the primary connectivity motif of third-order olfactory neurons indeed integrates signals, there still exist several labeled lines.
evidence: This is concluded from the connectivity analysis showing both integration and homotype-specific connections.

claim: A 'fovea' delineates deviations between experimentally observed connectivity matrices and connectivity under the assumption of random synapses in MB calyx, specifically for certain food-related uPNs.
source: In our study of the labeled-line strategy, we made several interesting observations, which are worth comparing with the concept of 'fovea' introduced by Zheng et al., 2020. A 'fovea' delineates deviations between experimentally observed connectivity matrices and connectivity under the assumption of random synapses in MB calyx, specifically for certain food-related uPNs (Zheng et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a concept from Zheng et al., 2020 that the authors compare with their findings.

claim: A subset of homotypic uPNs under the food-related 'fovea' reported by Zheng et al., 2020 are also spatially clustered.
source: A subset of homotypic uPNs under the food-related 'fovea' reported by Zheng et al., 2020 are also spatially clustered (e.g. DM1, DM4, DP1m, DP1l, VA2, and VA4).
evidence: This is observed from the clustering results and compared with findings from Zheng et al., 2020.

claim: It is likely that factors other than the spatial organization of uPNs in neuropils contribute to creating the 'fovea'.
source: Thus, it is likely that factors other than the spatial organization of uPNs in neuropils contribute to creating the 'fovea'.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that some homotypes under the 'fovea' are not spatially clustered together.

claim: The spatial proximity of pheromone-encoding homotypes in MB calyx may suggest the existence of pheromone-encoding 'fovea'.
source: Interestingly, the spatial proximity of pheromone-encoding homotypes in MB calyx may suggest the existence of pheromone-encoding 'fovea,' but most uPNs in these homotypes do not converge in connectivity-based clustering with an exception of VA1d.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed spatial clustering of pheromone-encoding homotypes.

claim: The spatial organization of pheromone-encoding homotypes in MB calyx, which is placed at the center of the neuropil, may facilitate the observed randomization of connections by increasing the accessibility of KCs to these homotypes.
source: In fact, we suspect the spatial organization of pheromone-encoding homotypes in MB calyx, which is placed at the center of the neuropil, to facilitate the observed randomization of connections by increasing the accessibility of KCs to these homotypes.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed spatial location of pheromone-encoding homotypes.

claim: There is a potential hygro/thermo 'fovea,' where homotypes such as VP1d and VP2 are spatially clustered together and the signals from these homotypes are relayed by the same set of KCs.
source: There is, however, a potential hygro/thermo 'fovea,' where homotypes such as VP1d and VP2 are spatially clustered together and the signals from these homotypes are relayed by the same set of KCs.
evidence: This is observed from the clustering and connectivity analysis.

claim: A large portion of mPNs is GABAergic and inhibitory.
source: A large portion of these mPNs is GABAergic and inhibitory (Berck et al., 2016; Tobin et al., 2017), whereas the role of interneurons can be both inhibitory and excitatory (Wilson et al., 2004; Turner et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Berck et al., 2016 and Tobin et al., 2017.

claim: Electrophysiological measurements indicate that mPNs are narrowly tuned to a specific set of odor stimuli.
source: Electrophysiological measurements indicate that mPNs are narrowly tuned to a specific set of odor stimuli (Berck et al., 2016), which is significant given that PNs are generally thought to be more broadly tuned than presynaptic ORNs (Wilson et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Berck et al., 2016 and Wilson et al., 2004.

claim: Several PNs do not follow the typical mALT, but mediolateral antennal lobe (mlALT) or lateral antennal lobe tracts (lALT) instead, thereby bypassing innervation through one of the higher olfactory centers.
source: Several PNs do not follow the typical mALT, but mediolateral antennal lobe (mlALT) or lateral antennal lobe tracts (lALT) instead, thereby bypassing innervation through one of the higher olfactory centers (Schultzhaus et al., 2017; Zheng et al., 2018; Bates et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schultzhaus et al., 2017, Zheng et al., 2018, and Bates et al., 2020.

claim: 28 uPNs present in the FAFB dataset are not explored in the study due to the selection criterion.
source: As stated previously, we confined ourselves to uPNs innervating all three neuropils to compare the spatial organization across neuropils for each uPN. As a result, 28 uPNs present in the FAFB dataset are not explored in our study.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the study's scope.

claim: The addition of 27 uPNs constituting 15 homotypes innervating LH but not MB calyx created four new clusters when hierarchical clustering was performed.
source: On the other hand, the addition of 27 uPNs constituting 15 homotypes innervating LH but not MB calyx created four new clusters when hierarchical clustering was performed (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The previously removed uPNs, most of which follow mlALT, are significantly different in terms of spatial and organizational characteristics and thus should be analyzed separately.
source: This suggests that the previously removed uPNs, most of which follow mlALT, are significantly different in terms of spatial and organizational characteristics and thus should be analyzed separately.
evidence: This is concluded from the increased d̄intra values when these uPNs are included.

claim: Out of 27 additional uPNs in LH, 21 were in mlALT, 5 were in trans-lALT, and 1 was in mALT.
source: Out of 27 additional uPNs in LH, 21 were in mlALT, 5 were in trans-lALT, and 1 was in mALT.
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of the additional uPNs.

claim: These 27 uPNs are mostly GABAergic (21 are labeled as GABAergic, 1 as cholinergic, and 4 as unknown neurotransmitter type), covering 84% of all GABAergic uPNs available in the FAFB dataset.
source: These 27 uPNs are mostly GABAergic (21 are labeled as GABAergic, 1 as cholinergic, and 4 as unknown neurotransmitter type), covering 84% of all GABAergic uPNs available in the FAFB dataset.
evidence: This is stated as a characterization of the additional uPNs.

claim: These uPNs innervate LH differently from other uPNs in the same homotype that follow mALT.
source: These uPNs innervate LH differently from other uPNs in the same homotype that follow mALT (see homotypes such as DA1, DC4, DL2d, DL2v, DP1l, VA1d, VA1v, VL2a, VL2p, and VP5 in Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Morphologically, inhibitory GABAergic neurons are often considered 'smooth' and aspiny.
source: Morphologically, inhibitory GABAergic neurons are often considered 'smooth' and aspiny (Douglas et al., 1989; Bopp et al., 2014; Gouwens et al., 2019), which are discernible from Figure 4—figure supplement 2.
evidence: This is supported by citations and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Many of the single-uPN homotypes, characterized by densely branched morphology, encode signals with aversive responses.
source: It is of great interest that many of the single-uPN homotypes, characterized by densely branched morphology, encode signals with aversive responses.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 6 and Figure 8.

claim: Direct transmission of the associated signals across the three neuropils via a single PN might simplify the overall processing of the olfactory signals as well as reduce the energetic cost.
source: Direct transmission of the associated signals across the three neuropils via a single PN might simplify the overall processing of the olfactory signals as well as reduce the energetic cost.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional significance of single-uPN homotypes.

claim: All uPN innervations within neuropil share a similar morphology regardless of the homotype.
source: Even though a structural difference exists between the single-uPN and multi-uPN homotypes, all uPN innervations within neuropil share a similar morphology regardless of the homotype (see Figure 6—figure supplement 1; Choi et al., 2022).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and cited from Choi et al., 2022.

claim: A localized morphological diversity within a neuron may be a characteristic aspect of pseudo-unipolar neurons like uPN and suggests a fundamentally multi-scale characteristic of neuron morphology.
source: A localized morphological diversity within a neuron may be a characteristic aspect of pseudo-unipolar neurons like uPN and suggests a fundamentally multi-scale characteristic of neuron morphology.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed morphological characteristics.

claim: The Drosophila brain EM reconstruction project has evolved to its near completion since the EM image dataset was first released.
source: The Drosophila brain EM reconstruction project has evolved to its near completion since the EM image dataset was first released (Dorkenwald et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dorkenwald et al., 2022.

claim: The reconstruction of the majority of the Drosophila central brain as well as the corresponding connectome with detailed information of the individual synapses has become publicly available.
source: The reconstruction of the majority of the Drosophila central brain as well as the corresponding connectome with detailed information of the individual synapses has become publicly available (Scheffer et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Scheffer et al., 2020.

claim: The analysis of the second-order neurons inside the Drosophila olfactory system may be translated to other parts of the nervous system in Drosophila as well as different organisms including the central nervous system (CNS) of humans.
source: Our analysis of the second-order neurons inside the Drosophila olfactory system may be translated to other parts of the nervous system in Drosophila as well as different organisms including the central nervous system (CNS) of humans.
evidence: This is a speculation about the broader applicability of the methods and findings.

claim: For the mammalian olfactory system, the details of analyses must be adapted, since the wiring scheme is much more complex than that of an insect.
source: For the mammalian olfactory system, the details of analyses must be adapted, however, since the wiring scheme is much more complex than that of an insect (Maresh et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Maresh et al., 2008.

claim: Multiple glomeruli encoding the same olfactory signal exist in humans.
source: For example, multiple glomeruli encoding the same olfactory signal exist in humans (Mombaerts et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mombaerts et al., 1996.

claim: According to the neurotransmitter map from a recent study, sophisticated processes beyond neuronal anatomy are apparently at work in the olfactory signal processing.
source: According to the neurotransmitter map from a recent study (Dolan et al., 2019), sophisticated processes beyond neuronal anatomy are apparently at work in the olfactory signal processing.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dolan et al., 2019.

claim: Functional studies incorporating odor response profiles in PNs and ORNs would supplement the findings of this study.
source: Thus, functional studies incorporating odor response profiles in PNs (Badel et al., 2016) and ORNs (Münch and Galizia, 2016; Bak et al., 2018) would supplement our findings.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future work supported by citations.

claim: The extension of this study to the other regulatory interneurons and mPNs, morphological studies of second-order neurons, and spatial analysis of third-order neurons will be of great interest for a better understanding of the olfactory signal processing beyond the implication of the neural anatomy and connectivity studied here.
source: The extension of our study to the other regulatory interneurons and mPNs, morphological studies of second-order neurons, and spatial analysis of third-order neurons will be of great interest for a better understanding of the olfactory signal processing beyond the implication of the neural anatomy and connectivity studied here.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future work.

claim: 135 uPNs constituting 57 homotypes were collected from the FAFB dataset under the criterion that uPNs innervate all three neuropils.
source: Thus, out of 164 uPNs, a total of 135 uPNs constituting 57 homotypes were collected under this criteria, resulting in mostly cholinergic uPNs that follow mALT.
evidence: This is stated as part of the data preparation methods.

claim: 120 uPNs forming 58 glomeruli were collected from the hemibrain dataset based on the same criterion used for the FAFB dataset.
source: The hemibrain dataset (Scheffer et al., 2020) was taken from the neuPrint database (Clements et al., 2020), where we collected from the right hemisphere of the female Drosophila a total of 120 uPNs forming 58 glomeruli based on the same criterion we used for the FAFB dataset (uPNs that innervate all three neuropils).
evidence: This is stated as part of the data preparation methods.

claim: The discrepancy in the number of uPNs between the two datasets most likely resulted from the difference between the neuropil boundary used and the region defined by the hemibrain dataset.
source: The discrepancy in the number of uPNs between the two datasets most likely resulted from the difference between the neuropil boundary we used and the region defined by the hemibrain dataset.
evidence: This is an inference about the cause of the discrepancy.

claim: The total number of uPNs in both datasets is comparable, with 164 uPNs in the FAFB dataset and 162 uPNs in the hemibrain dataset.
source: In fact, we find that the total number of uPNs in both datasets is comparable, with 164 uPNs in the FAFB dataset and 162 uPNs in the hemibrain dataset.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: A recent community-led effort identified three glomeruli in both databases with conflicting glomerulus labels.
source: Additionally, a recent community-led effort identified three glomeruli in both databases with conflicting glomerulus labels, which have been a source of confusion (Schlegel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schlegel et al., 2021.

claim: The community agreed to rename the glomeruli in both datasets labeled as VC3l, VC3m, and VC5 as VC3, VC5, and VM6, respectively.
source: After an extensive study, the community agreed to rename the glomeruli in both datasets labeled as VC3l, VC3m, and VC5 as VC3, VC5, and VM6, respectively (Schlegel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schlegel et al., 2021.

claim: The boundaries defining each neuropil were systematically chosen from local minima that separate neuropils from rigid backbones.
source: The boundaries defining each neuropil were systematically chosen from local minima that separate neuropils from rigid backbones.
evidence: This is stated as part of the neuropil segmentation methodology.

claim: The neuropil segmentation boundaries are comparable with neuropil volume surface coordinates provided by Ito et al., 2014 via CATMAID.
source: We compared our neuropil segmentation boundaries with neuropil volume surface coordinates provided by Ito et al., 2014 via CATMAID (Saalfeld et al., 2009) and found the boundaries are comparable (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as a validation of the segmentation method.

claim: 1754 KCs and 1295 LHNs were chosen that made at least three synaptic connections with any of the 120 uPNs from the hemibrain dataset.
source: We chose KCs and LHNs that made at least three synaptic connections with any of the 120 uPNs from the hemibrain dataset. This resulted in 1754 KCs and 1295 LHNs, creating bipartite connectivity matrices at each neuropil.
evidence: This is stated as part of the connectivity analysis methodology.
